sources.title: Malaysia’s Melaka poll begins as 79 cleared in test for Anwar’s coalition
Melaka state election: Anwar's PH, Muhyiddin's Bersatu avoid clashes in 4 seats as candidates confirmed

en.title: Melaka state election campaign begins with 79 candidates cleared
en.dek: Melaka election campaign starts; 79 candidates contest 28 seats, testing coalition dynamics.
facts: 79 candidates cleared to contest 28 seats in Melaka
Bersatu will contest 7 seats, avoiding direct contests in four seats with PH
BN will contest 23 seats and PN 5 seats after resolving a seat allocation dispute with MCA
The election will feature 11 straight fights, 11 three‑cornered contests, and six four‑cornered contests
body: The Election Commission announced on 31 October that the campaign for the 16th Melaka state election had begun. The announcement followed the confirmation of all 79 candidates on nomination day. The campaign will run until the polls on 14 November. The state is located south of Kuala Lumpur.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition will contest 24 of the 28 seats. Former premier Muhyiddin Yassin’s Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) will contest seven seats and has avoided direct contests in four seats with PH. Analysts said the nominations show PH and Bersatu are informally cooperating, though some internal pushback means they have not explicitly admitted it.

United Malays National Organisation (Umno) and Pan-Malaysian Islamic Party (PAS) are part of the Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) partnership. BN will contest 23 seats in partnership with PN, which will contest the remaining five seats. The BN‑PN partnership began when PAS called on its supporters to support BN at the Johor state election in July.

The Malaysian Chinese Association (MCA) had threatened to derail the alliance after it said it was unsatisfied with the number of seats it was allocated. The dispute was resolved after eleventh‑hour talks between the two coalitions, when MCA was given two additional seats – Bandar Hilir and Kota Laksamana – to contest.

Analysts told CNA that the nominations show PH and Bersatu are informally cooperating, although some internal pushback from at least one component party means they have not explicitly admitted it. Future cooperation depends on whether Bersatu can help PH win some of the Malay votes in Melaka and stem the “Malay tsunami”, the analysts said.

The 79 candidates will contest 28 seats, with 11 straight fights, 11 three‑cornered contests, and six four‑cornered contests. The election will test whether Anwar Ibrahim’s coalition can work with Islamist opponents to gain national power.
en.context: The election is a test of whether Anwar Ibrahim’s governing partners can turn an opportunistic alliance with Islamist opponents into a platform for national power. Melaka is a coastal state south of Kuala Lumpur. The campaign begins on 31 October and the polls are on 14 November.
en.imageCaption: Pakatan Harapan chairman Anwar Ibrahim (left) and Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia president Muhyiddin Yassin. (Photos: Facebook/Anwar Ibrahim, Muhyiddin Yassin)
